children: Commodity markets traded mixed on September 4, with oil prices rising and heading for their strongest weekly gain since mid-July, while gold held steady and was poised for a modest weekly gain.
Oil prices rose on Friday and are on track for the steepest weekly gain since mid-July as rising tensions and renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities heightened concerns over Middle East supply risks.
Brent crude futures rose 15 cents, or 0.2%, to $95.67 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures were up 26 cents, or 0.3%, at $91.56.
On a weekly basis, Brent rose 7.1% and WTI was 9.8% higher, set for the highest gains since the week ended July 20.
Gold held steady on Friday and was poised for a small weekly gain, as attention turned to highly awaited U.S. payrolls data for clues on the Federal Reserve's next interest rate decision.

Spot gold held its ground at $4,477.10 per ounce. Prices jumped 2% on Thursday as traders scaled back expectations for a September rate hike after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would support leaving rates unchanged if data continued to show inflation pressures moderating.
U.S. gold futures for December delivery fell 0.4% to $4,522.60.
Among other precious metals, silver was up 0.1% at $66.90 an ounce. Platinum and palladium were little changed.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, fell 0.05% to 99.54. The euro edged up 0.02% to $1.1589, while the yen strengthened 0.07% to 158.59 per dollar, following a 0.9% surge in the prior session.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil climbs on supply risks; gold holds steady ahead of US jobs data
